content.comment_body: Could someone review my program and offer some advice? I'm having a hard time figuring this out and could use some guidance. The oven is controlled by a set point, which is a user-defined variable entered on the [product_name] operator device, so the set point isn't always the same. What I need is for a timer to be activated when the temperature reaches the set point. For example: temperature = 100°C, set point = 150°C. When the temperature reaches 150°C, an output will indicate that the oven is at temperature, and a countdown timer can be activated by an input. Once the time has elapsed, another output should turn on. However, after timing out, the timer should be able to start again, as long as the temperature is still at the set point. To summarize, the timer should ONLY be activated if the temperature has reached the set point. As mentioned, I'm struggling to make this work, so any guidance would be greatly appreciated.
Is this the kind of setup you had in mind?

analysis.insight_summary: The user is working to implement a timer that only activates and can be restarted when the oven's temperature matches a user-defined set point, using [company_name] hardware/software. The main challenge is linking the temperature condition to the timer's operation and reset logic, with current difficulties affecting progress.
analysis.user_expectations: The user is looking for clear advice or example programming logic that ensures the timer activates and restarts strictly when the temperature equals the set point, to improve both reliability and usability of the oven control program.
pain_keywords: inability to link user variable and logic
